title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (Q4 2027)
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: Comprehensive product documentation for the Unified Inference product family: product overview, PRD and requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap and themes through Q4 2027, pricing and packaging guidance, and most recent release notes.
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Product Requirements Document (PRD), high-level design, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference. It is intended for engineering, product, sales, and customer-facing teams who need a single reference for product scope, priorities, constraints, and operational readiness.

Key goals
- Provide a single, consistent inference API and operational model across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Reduce customer unit costs while preserving latency SLOs and output quality.
- Enable predictable enterprise adoption via SLAs, observability, and rollout controls.

Audience and ownership
- Primary: product, eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, eng-sre, sales-enablement.
- Document owner: Product (Sofia Martinez).
- Engineering owners: Runtime (Marcus Lee), Platform (Aisha Patel).

1) Product requirements (PRD)

Scope
- Core surface: text generation, chat (multi-turn), embeddings, reranking, and structured output.
- Deployment surfaces: Hosted API (public), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Key capabilities: streaming, function/tool calling, prefix & KV caching, model variants & quantization profiles, cost-aware routing.

Success metrics (OKRs)
- Customer adoption: 30 new Dedicated customers and 12 Private deals in FY2027.
- Reliability: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated and Hosted control-plane; 99.9% for compute-backed serving.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency for small requests < 150ms (hosted), median throughput uplift 1.8x vs baseline via batching/caching.
- Cost: 20% average unit cost reduction for customers adopting Redwood Optimize recommendations within 3 months.

Non‑goals
- Full MLOps training pipelines (out of scope — integrations will be via reference connectors).
- Model training or model ownership — we do not host model training in the product.

Constraints and assumptions
- Support for popular open models (Llama2-style, MPT, Falcon variants) plus quantized variants (INT8/4 where available).
- Customers will supply model artifacts for Private; packaging constraints limited to supported OS/distributions per onprem-packaging docs.

Requirements (high-level table)
| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Owner | Acceptance criteria |
| REQ-PRD-001 | Unified REST/SDK API for text, chat, embeddings | P0 | Product | Same calls across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; SDKs updated; examples in quickstarts |
| REQ-PRD-002 | Per-route SLOs & fallbacks | P0 | Eng-platform | Canary & auto-fallback to variant; SLO eval dashboard |
| REQ-PRD-003 | Cost-aware routing & recommendations | P1 | Product/Optimize | Routing policies by cost/latency; Optimize recommendations exported as playbooks |
| REQ-PRD-004 | Quantization profiles & verification | P1 | Eng-serving-runtime | Profile catalog; perf regressions <= 5% vs baseline; documented regressions in regressions-triage |
| REQ-PRD-005 | Observability: token-level cost, per-route tracing | P0 | Eng-platform | Dashboards, alerts, 90-day retention for product teams |

User flows (examples)
1. Self-serve hosted onboarding: signup -> free credits -> quickstart template (chat) -> first 100k tokens instrumented for cost analytics.
2. Dedicated provisioning: enterprise signs commitment -> capacity plan -> pool creation -> model pinning and canary rollout -> SLA activation.
3. Private deployment: customer provisions VPC connector -> onprem package install -> control-plane pairing -> key management & audit logging enabled.

2) Design and architecture highlights

High‑level architecture
- Control plane: tenant management, model catalog, routing policies, billing triggers, rollout controls.
- Data plane: high-throughput GPU runtime (continuous batching, KV cache management) with kernel selection layer.
- Observability & Optimize: token-level metering, quality monitoring (evals), recommendations engine.

Design tradeoffs & rationale
- Batching vs latency: default small-request fast-path (no batching) for low p95 latency; user-configurable batching for throughput-sensitive routes.
- Quantization verification: accept small quality regressions only if within configured thresholds; auto-rollbacks on regression alerts.

API surface (important endpoints and fields)
- POST /v1/generate (params: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, stop, stream)
- POST /v1/chat (params: model, messages[], functions[], function_call)
- POST /v1/embeddings (params: model, input)
- GET /v1/models (model metadata, quantization profiles, perf_profile)
- Routing policy config (UI/CLI) fields: preferred_region, cost_tier, latency_slo_ms, fallback_chain (list of model ids)

Config table: example config keys
| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| routing.latency_slo_ms | integer | 150 | Target p95 latency for route (ms) |
| routing.cost_priority | string | balanced | Options: cost | latency | balanced |
| optimize.enabled | boolean | true | Enable Optimize recommendations for account |
| runtime.kv_cache_enabled | boolean | true | Enable KV/prefix cache for chat sessions |

Telemetry and QA
- Metrics: tokens_served, requests_per_min, p50/p90/p95 latency, model_fallback_count, quantization_regressions, cost_per_1k_tokens.
- Traces: per-request trace id injected and propagated to runtime and billing.
- Quality: evals tied to prompt sets; regression alerts trigger regression-triage process.

Security & compliance notes
- Private: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM (integrations documented) and audit-logging.
- Data residency: routing policies honor region residency constraints.

3) Roadmap & themes (Q4 2027 planning window)

Themes by quarter (high level)
- Q3 2027 (completed): Dedicated autoscaling v1, Optimize MVP recommendations, initial Private onprem packaging.
- Q4 2027 (current): Quantization profiles catalog expansion, per-route cost SLOs, SLA improvements for Dedicated, release of unified SDK v3.
- Q1 2028 (planned): Advanced batching controls, adaptive routing (real-time cost/latency tradeoffs), integrations with third-party KMS vendors.
- Q2 2028 (planned): Privacy-focused onprem enhancements (air-gapped installer), expanded model catalog (LLM family additions), self-serve Dedicated provisioning.

Roadmap milestones & owners
- Milestone: Quantization catalog v1 (due 2027-10-15) — Owner: Eng-serving-runtime (Marcus Lee)
- Milestone: Per-route cost SLOs (due 2027-11-30) — Owner: Eng-platform (Aisha Patel)
- Milestone: Unified SDK v3 release (due 2027-12-15) — Owner: Eng-developer-experience

Dependencies & risks
- Dependency: GPU kernel improvements from external vendor may change perf baselines — risk mitigation: maintain kernel compatibility layer and fallback profiles.
- Risk: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization — mitigation: staged rollout and automated rollback thresholds.

4) Pricing & packaging notes

Packaging tiers (summary)
- Hosted (Self-serve): usage-based pricing (per-token generation, per-embedding unit), free tier for first 100k tokens and 1k embeddings.
- Dedicated (Reserved capacity): monthly/annual capacity commitments with SKU-based GPU pools and optional burst credits.
- Private (Enterprise): platform license + deployment fee + optional support/retention addons.

Pricing guidance (examples)
- Hosted generation: $0.0009 per token (base model), optimized variants: $0.0006 per token (quantized).
- Embeddings: $0.0015 per embedding (hosted).
- Dedicated: list price depends on pool size; sample: 4xA100 pool + management = $35k/month for baseline entry tier.

Discounts & packaging rules
- Volume discounts start at $250k ARR for Hosted usage; Dedicated committed contracts include tiered discounts based on 12/24/36 month terms.
- Pricing change policy: 90-day notice for significant pricing changes for customers with active commitments.

Cost-saving levers to communicate to customers
- Use Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization profile, model variant routing).
- Pin workloads to cheaper regions or dedicated pools for predictable throughput.

5) Release notes (most recent production release)

Release: Unified Inference v2027-08-25 (rolling production release)
- Highlights:
  - Quantization profiles (alpha) for 4 popular open models; first verified INT8 profiles with perf improvements up to 2.1x.
  - Dedicated autoscaling improvements (reduced scale-up time 30%).
  - Streaming API enhancements: function call streaming and faster reconnect semantics.
- Bug fixes:
  - Fixed incorrect token accounting for batched ephemeral sessions (billing discrepancy).
  - Resolved rare deadlock in KV cache eviction path under heavy multi-tenant loads.
- Upgrade notes:
  1. SDKs: clients should upgrade to unified SDK v2.7+ to get streaming fix.
  2. Dedicated customers: no downtime expected for autoscaler improvements; capacity reconfiguration recommended during maintenance window.

Rollout and rollback plan
- Canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours with automated regression checks on latency, error rate, and cost-per-token.
- Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days if no regressions.
- Automated rollback if p95 latency increases > 20% or error-rate increase > 0.5% sustained for 30 minutes.

Operational runbooks & next steps
- See runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks for per-route SLO configuration and canary playbook.
- Action items for next quarter: finalize quantization catalog v1, complete SDK v3 feature parity, and update pricing pages in sales-enablement.
